verdict.rationale: kitty's first-party remote-control docs describe controlling the terminal from scripts or the shell: opening windows, sending arbitrary text, and changing window and tab titles, over a documented socket interface. A hands-on runtime probe on kitty 0.48.2 independently confirmed the whole loop: `kitten @ ls` returned window, tab and layout state as JSON, `send-text` executed in the live window, `get-text` read the output back, and `close-window` tore it down. Every element of the story (open windows, send text, query state) is covered by in-depth docs plus hands-on verification.
